subject: Agriculture
title: Mycotoxins and Food Safety
description: Learn Mycotoxins and Food Safety in one minute.

hook.text: Aflatoxin, produced by a common grain mold, is one of the most potent carcinogens known. It contaminates 25% of crops.

buildup.text: Aspergillus fungi grow on corn, peanuts, and tree nuts—especially in warm, humid storage conditions.

discovery.text: Chronic low-dose aflatoxin exposure causes liver cancer. In developing countries, it kills 30,000 people annually.

twist.text: Rich countries test and reject contaminated grain. Poor countries eat it because they can't afford to throw food away.

climax.text: Biocontrol fungi—harmless Aspergillus strains that outcompete toxin producers—are showing promise in Africa.

punchline.text: The mold is invisible. The cancer takes decades. The poorest pay the price.

quiz.question: What health effect does chronic aflatoxin exposure cause?
